# 05: One typed command changes any setting

**What to build:** the settings window changes every setting through one typed command. Today each setting has its own `set_*` command, `build.rs` entry, capability and autogenerated permission, plus a TS `Field` name kept by hand.

**Blocked by:** 04 (it adds ts-rs and the drift test).

**Status:** ready-for-agent

## Decisions

- One command `update_setting(change: SettingChange)`. `SettingChange` is a serde-tagged enum with one variant per field, notification fields split (ShowMessages, ShowSender, SoundEnabled, SoundPath), download path included. Bad input fails to deserialize.
- `update_setting` maps to one core Event. It replaces the 11 `set_*` commands and their `build.rs` entries, capabilities and autogenerated permissions.
- Only `capabilities/settings.json` grants `update_setting`. `remote.json` does not change.
- `set_chat_list_width` stays a separate command, because the untrusted account page calls it.
- ts-rs also exports `SettingChange`, with the same drift test.
- The TS `Field` union goes. Save errors point at the `SettingChange` tag. Account errors keep their own name.

## Done when

- [ ] Adding a boolean setting needs: a `Settings` field, a `SettingsView` field, a `SettingChange` variant, a core handler line, and the control in `panes.tsx`.
- [ ] Core tests cover each `SettingChange` variant.
- [ ] The drift test and `pnpm --dir frontend build` pass.
- [ ] Manual check in the bundled app: each control in Settings saves, survives a restart, and a failed save shows its error under the right control.
